limitaciones.intro: The slope of each stint is what the tyre «seems» to lose per lap, not its real wear. The data can't correct for these:
limitaciones.trafico: Traffic: running behind another car costs time that has nothing to do with the tyre.
limitaciones.pista: Temperature and track evolution: the surface gets faster with each lap and can hide wear, as happened in Qatar 2024.
limitaciones.combustible: Fuel: the correction uses {segundos, number} s per lap for every car, which is an approximation.
limitaciones.limpias: Only clean laps count: the first lap, safety car or flag laps, pit entry and exit laps and very slow ones are dropped.

limitaciones.titulo: What this analysis does not measure
limitaciones.intro: The delta says who was faster and where, with these caveats:
limitaciones.muestras: Few samples: public telemetry has about 3.7 per second, one every ~20 m at 250 km/h.
limitaciones.picos: Bumps in slow corners: the delta goes up and comes back down at heavy braking zones. That is partly sampling noise and the misalignment between the two laps; what matters is the level it settles at after the corner. To reduce it the delta is averaged over ~100 m windows, which removes the jaggedness but also rounds off real, sudden changes.
limitaciones.exactitud: Accuracy: the final delta is exact because it is fitted to each lap official time. Mid-lap it is off by about 0.04 s on average (0.13 s at most) against the official sector times.
limitaciones.porque: It does not say why: it shows who was faster in a stretch, not whether it was braking later, a better line or lifting off.
limitaciones.condiciones: Different conditions: with no segment picked, each driver uses their best lap of the session, which may come from another moment, on another tyre or with more fuel. Traffic is not corrected.
limitaciones.tramos: The stretches have equal length; they are not the official mini-sectors of the broadcast.
